claim.spatial_precision: Paraguayan Chaco ranch contexts; country entity is index only
claim.summary: An ILO investigation in the Paraguayan Chaco confirmed forced labour on a minority of traditional ranches and described labour relations in many of those cases as debt bondage. The evidence is explicitly non-uniform and geographically bounded to ranch contexts in the Chaco, so the atlas records a positive debt-bondage claim for the documented 2005 investigation without extending it to Paraguay as a whole.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim d22ed3c9-0c71-4569-80da-c367459c3bde into current post-M1 semantics. No new P-level is assigned. Legacy geometry b37bbfed-4916-4d94-a671-5ac3d5a21f69 is an explicit modern/navigation proxy and is not promoted as this claim's historical/practice inference extent.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded classification only. Do not infer national prevalence, uniform territorial distribution, legal status, or a country-wide practice polygon beyond what the evidence directly supports.

source.title: Debt servitude and marginalization in the Chaco of Paraguay
source.author_or_institution: Alvaro Bedoya Silva-Santisteban; Eduardo Bedoya Garland
source.geographic_scope: Paraguayan Chaco, especially traditional remote cattle ranches
source.independence_notes: ILO-commissioned investigation. Treat interviews, inspector findings and report narrative as one evidence family rather than independent votes.
source.reliability_limitations: The report explicitly says forced labour existed on a minority of Chaco ranches. It does not support a national prevalence estimate or a whole-country practice extent.
